Environmental reporting suffers from a "standardization crisis": two-thirds omitted emissions data, while over half failed to report renewable energy metrics, while those reporting used incompatible measurement units (tCO₂ versus tCO₂e), precluding meaningful comparison. Through an institutional theory lens, results indicate that clear coercive regulatory pressures drive compliance on simple ratio-based targets, but insufficient mimetic and normative forces undermine comprehensive transparency. detail.abstract: This study constructs a reproducible policy laboratory for crime and violence reduction in Bolivia using a path-dependent agent-based microsimulation calibrated to the 2025 Household Survey and the fourth-quarter 2025 Continuous Employment Survey. The objective is not to forecast crime mechanically or to identify a single universally superior intervention. It is to represent multiple mechanisms through which victimization, offending, severe violence, reporting, institutional legitimacy, spatial displacement, criminal adaptation, and policy capacity can evolve jointly, and then to compare portfolios under explicit structural and calibration uncertainty. The model combines a survey-weighted synthetic population created from official expansion factors and cross-survey donor matching, heterogeneous routine exposure, prior victimization and offending, socioeconomic shocks, place risk, illicit-network pressure, community organization, police and justice capacity, municipal instruments, social programs, and criminal adaptation. Policy modules include hot-spots policing, problem-oriented policing, focused deterrence, procedural justice, community social control, Guardabosquestype conditional collective incentives, youth and adult behavioral interventions, employment and school-retention measures, street lighting and place remediation, alcohol regulation, violence interruption, witness protection, homicide investigation, financialnetwork disruption, rehabilitation, and oversight. Empirical targets are kept separate from external intervention priors and structural assumptions. The baseline ABM ensemble is emulated by an adaptive stack combining Gaussian processes with a Bayesianbootstrap tree ensemble; global sensitivity is examined with Sobol and active-subspace methods; baseline structural parameters are calibrated using a tempered ensemble MCMC with adaptive covariance preconditioning; and policy scenarios are propagated through posterior, intervention-prior, and structural uncertainty. In the included development run, the 2025 Household Survey implies a weighted 12-month victimization rate of 13.65%, formal reporting of 16.91% among victims, normalized police trust of 0.470, and normalized perceived safety of 0.488. The fully integrated package reduces simulated victimization by 17.9% relative to a paired baseline, with a 5th-95th percentile range of approximately 15.1-20.9%; focused place-based packages achieve similar but lower-cost reductions while enforcement-heavy portfolios generate larger displacement. Community-control and Guardabosques-type modules produce smaller national-average effects because the model deliberately treats their strongest evidence as local and conditional rather than universal. These figures are model-conditional scenario outputs, not causal estimates for Bolivia. The principal contribution is an auditable architecture for testing combinations, trade-offs, and failure modes before policy scale-up.

detail.abstract:
A direct-indexing separately managed account harvests a great deal of loss in its first year and steadily less every year after. As winners accumulate embedded gains, fewer lots sit below cost basis, and the decay can be predicted on the day the account is funded. We give it a closed form. If each holding's log-moneyness is a Brownian motion with drift, a fresh lot is harvested only if it ever reaches the loss threshold, which happens with probability p = exp(-2mh/sigma^2). That one number fixes a finite lifetime budget of p/(1-p) harvests per name and a defective renewal equation for the harvest rate. A density transfer operator integrates the aging curve and a fixed-seed Monte Carlo checks it name by name: at a base calibration the year-one harvest yield is 20.3% of NAV (analytic) against 19.5% (simulated), the year-ten yield is 2.8% against 2.7%, and nearly a quarter of the twenty-year harvest is realized in year one.

The refresh of basis is then posed as an impulse-control problem. A partial liquidation, a charitable flush of low-basis lots, or a 351 conversion pays a tax or transaction cost now and restores the fresh harvest curve. Because the value of a harvested loss is capped by how much outside gain the client can shelter in a year, the account should be reset when its decayed yield falls to a level set by the reset cost, the discount rate, and that loss value. Under a base calibration that means a reset about every seven years for a client with ordinary short-term outside gains, sooner when those gains are abundant, and never when they are scarce or when the exit is a step-up in basis. Higher single-name volatility and larger contribution flow both delay the reset; a larger appetite for outside gains brings it forward.

detail.abstract: Large language models improve the renegotiation of distressed financial contracts. detail.abstract: Wind, solar and nuclear plants are paid for before they generate, so the price of money decides much of what they cost. Across Europe the price of that capital differs sharply between countries. The cost of capital reported for renewable projects runs from 1.93 per cent in Germany to 10.59 in Latvia, and an independent survey five years earlier found a similar crosscountry ordering across twenty-five countries. The gap opens where money reaches the project, in how much a bank will lend and what the equity that fills the rest demands, rather than in sovereign borrowing, where the countries lay much closer together over the same years. This paper asks why a single electricity market has not produced a single market for financing the plants that supply it, and sets the question against the history of how those plants were paid for. The historical cases document five financing routes, utility balance sheets, state capital, consumer prepayment, offtaker consortia and plan allocation, drawn here from appraisals, government bills and company accounts. They differ in where the capital came from but share an institutional route through which long-lived investment could be repaid. Liberalisation separated those functions between 1995 and 2010 rather than abolishing them, and in three documented cases a country's financing regime had already changed once as its earlier fleet accumulated assets and cash flow. The instruments that followed restore parts of that arrangement and not the whole: contracts can protect a project's revenue, public lending can lower the cost of its debt, guarantees can absorb named risks and grants can cut the capital it must raise, and none of them by itself reproduces the financing capacity of an established utility with a cost-recovering customer base. Countries entered the liberalised market with different amounts of capital already paid for and different amounts left to finance on market terms. Since 2010 the building has shifted towards the countries that had built least, and the available project evidence reports several of them financing with less debt and more equity. Completing the transition takes more than mobilising a larger quantity of capital. The unresolved question is whether comparable projects can obtain comparable terms across countries when the revenue protection, the debt capacity and the risk-bearing functions once combined inside a utility are supplied separately and project by project.

detail.abstract: The conflict that erupted in Khartoum on 15 April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has precipitated the most severe state collapse in modern Sudanese history. Drawing on first-hand eyewitness observation from Khartoum between April 2023 and March 2024, World Bank Sudan Economic Update May 2025 data (World Bank, 2025), Worldwide Governance Indicators (World Bank, 2023), and classical political theory from Ibn Khaldun (1377/2015) and Immanuel Kant (1793/1996), this article develops an institutional explanation for Sudan's disintegration. The central argument is that three decades of systemic state capture under the National Congress Party (1989-2019) produced a praetorian militia whose economic base rested on gold misinvoicing and violent entrepreneurship rather than legitimate taxation (Hellman et al., 2000; de Waal, 2019; Baldo, 2017). Official World Bank (2025) figures document contraction of real GDP by 29.4% in 2023 and further 13.5% in 2024, rise in extreme poverty from 33% in 2022 to 71% in 2024, unemployment from 32% to 47%, year-on-year inflation of 170% in 2024, and 12.9 million forcibly displaced persons, the largest displacement crisis recorded globally (World Bank, 2025; UNHCR, 2024). The paper deconstructs RSF's claim to restore democracy by showing its campaign has systematically destroyed institutional prerequisites for polyarchy identified by Dahl (1989) and Diamond (1999). It introduces Kessiba (bounty) economy as roving banditry that never transitions to stationary governance (Olson, 1993; Volkov, 2002) and applies Kant's (1793) notion of radical evil, as interpreted by Allison (1990, 1996), to practices such as slave markets, systematic sexual violence, and deliberate severing of telecommunications to block remittances. Material damages are inventoried at over USD 150 billion as of November 2023, including 63 research centers, National Documentary Centre, 1,224 factories, 360,000 vehicles, and 60,000 houses. Five future trajectories are modeled. The analysis concludes that without UN Chapter VII-authorized stabilization force, global trusteeship, educational reform, and demilitarization, Sudan will remain incubator for transnational insecurity in Red Sea and Sahel.

detail.abstract: Embodied Biographical Alignment (EBA) investigates whether the integration of multiple, finite, developmentally structured biographies can be used as a source of alignment-relevant learning for an artificial system. This note treats existing studies not as tests of EBA, but as sources of experimental results, methods, and constructions that intersect with particular components of its research question. Work on knowledge distillation, representation and policy transfer, path dependence, sequential reinforcement learning, continual learning, and training-state transfer shows that artificial systems can transfer more than final outputs; that similar performance does not guarantee matching internal mechanisms or represented information; that training history can leave persistent internal differences and influence subsequent learning and generalization; and that some causally relevant consequences of history can be retained in identifiable components of training state and transferred between systems. For EBA, these results form a map of existing experimental possibilities. On this basis, the note introduces an operational question of developmental equivalence: is reproducing a system's current functional state sufficient, or does reproducing its subsequent learning, adaptation, and generalization require preserving additional causally relevant consequences of its developmental history?

detail.abstract: The integration of Emergency Arbitrators (EAs) into international arbitration rules, particularly those of the ICC, has transformed the landscape of urgent dispute resolution. However, the enforcement of these measures in jurisdictions with distinct legal traditions, such as the Islamic Republic of Iran, remains fraught with practical and procedural complexities. This paper critically examines the enforceability of ICC emergency orders within the Iranian legal system. By analyzing the interplay between the 1958 New York Convention, Iranian procedural law, and the doctrine of public policy (ordre public), this study demonstrates why the direct enforcement of EA orders as final “awards” is legally problematic. Conversely, it proposes a strategic framework for practitioners: leveraging these orders as compelling evidentiary support for equivalent interim relief applications under the Iranian Code of Civil Procedure (Articles 310 et seq.). This approach offers a viable, compliant pathway to securing urgent relief in cross-border disputes involving Iranian parties.

detail.abstract: Do investors act consistently on their beliefs when they trade? We study this question in a controlled trading experiment that jointly elicits return forecasts and trading decisions. We document a distinct behavioral friction: a belief--action gap, whereby choices become less responsive to beliefs. This gap is concentrated in selling decisions involving paper losses: investors liquidate losing positions in a much noisier and less belief-responsive manner. Using a probabilistic choice framework, we separate the belief--action gap from shifts in risk tolerance and belief biases and show that it is a major source of trading underperformance. Finally, we implement an automated selling mechanism that removes discretionary selling. Automated selling restores belief--action consistency and substantially improves profitability, indicating that reluctance to realize losses reflects a behavioral failure to act on information rather than optimal risk-taking.

detail.abstract: Developing countries have followed a policy of manufacturing export-led economic growth to some success during the twentieth century, and in the process have become richer and more developed. My GMM estimation with data from 61 developing countries in 1960 across 60 years shows that GDP growth is positively associated with, and in turn dynamically affects export share of consumer and capital goods, import share of capital goods and education. detail.abstract: Loss-of-chance damages are conventionally computed as the probability that a wrongful act caused an opportunity to be lost, multiplied by the value of that opportunity. This paper argues that in competition-law cases built on exclusionary conduct, where the lost opportunity is participation in an oligopoly, the value term cannot be treated the way the classical framework treats it: it is not a fixed benchmark read off incumbents' observed profits, but an equilibrium outcome of a counterfactual market structure that does not exist in the data, so recovering it requires reconstructing that market rather than observing it. The probability term raises no comparable difficulty; it is the ordinary survival probability any new entrant faces. I develop this argument with a fully worked example of deterred entry, calibrated so the model's implied number of surviving firms matches the number observed, and show that benchmarking the lost opportunity's value off incumbents' profits produces a large, quantifiable overstatement of damages. I then integrate the game-theoretic literature on strategic entry deterrence, which explains how exclusionary conduct manipulates that value, with the structural econometric literature on entry and market structure, which supplies the means of recovering it, into a protocol for estimating loss-of-chance damages in practice.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a two-sector dynamic general-equilibrium model with heterogeneous households and endogenous pollution to evaluate four fiscal instruments—production-based pollution taxes, consumption-based environmental taxes, labor income taxes, and capital income taxes—under multiple policy objectives. The analysis shows that instruments designed for one objective generate important spillovers onto others: environmental taxes affect income distribution and welfare, while income taxes influence environmental quality. Clear trade-offs emerge, as gains in environmental quality or equality are accompanied by lower employment, capital, and output; no instrument achieves inclusive growth. The ranking of instruments depends systematically on households’ environmental awareness, the elasticity of substitution between goods, and sectoral factor intensities. These findings imply that the choice of fiscal instrument should be guided by the structural characteristics of the economy rather than by conventional tax classifications.

detail.abstract: Jointly produced exhaustible resources are commonly modeled as if the common ore were homogeneous, although real mines move through domains with different yields, costs, and continuation values. detail.abstract: Can the rapid expansion of e-commerce delivery services be macroeconomically compatible with---or even complementary to---circular-economy objectives? Answering this question requires a framework in which delivery intensity, recycling behaviour, and aggregate production are jointly determined. This paper provides such a framework by developing a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) model in which households jointly choose delivery service intensity and recycling effort, trading off the convenience of home delivery against waste generation and the time cost of in-store shopping. Recycled materials enter a constant elasticity of substitution (CES) composite that substitutes for virgin inputs in production, linking consumer recycling behaviour directly to aggregate output. The central contribution is a novel income-effect mechanism: a positive total factor productivity (TFP) shock raises real income and reduces optimal market working hours; because recycling effort and market labour share the same effective time aggregate, the fall in working hours lowers the marginal cost of recycling effort, inducing households to raise the recycling rate. Productivity growth thus simultaneously expands output and strengthens circular-economy activity through the same income channel---an endogenous complementarity absent from existing circular-economy DSGE models. The model is calibrated to an annual frequency and solved by log-linearisation using the RISE Toolbox (Maih2015). Three sensitivity analyses confirm the robustness of the income-effect mechanism and reveal a development-stage asymmetry: under a mature recycling norm, income-driven recycling effort crowds out delivery expansion, whereas a direct norm shock generates a green supply-side expansion---simultaneous gains in output, recycling, labour, and environmental quality---at both norm calibrations.

detail.abstract: Trust that extends beyond a narrow circle of people helps sustain modern societies and can facilitate cross-border economic exchange and collective action on global challenges such as climate change and pandemics. Across societies, however, individuals’ trust is bounded, and trust that extends beyond common social boundaries is weaker than trust in socially-proximate others. This paper argues that cross-cultural variation in these boundaries of trust, measured as trust in other nationalities, is partly rooted in societal differences in ethnonational primordialism (the belief that national belonging is fundamentally fixed by inherited characteristics such as ancestry and birthplace), independent of primordialism’s effect on the general propensity to trust. I test this argument using individual-level survey data covering 36-52 countries, depending on the specification and empirical approach. Trust in other nationalities is consistently lower in societies with stronger ethnonational primordialist beliefs, including when controlling for cultural individualism/collectivism and kinship intensity, two established predictors of the scope of trust. Evidence from an epidemiological approach using second-generation migrants is also consistent with a causal interpretation. The results point to beliefs about the basis of national membership as an important additional cultural predictor of how far trust extends beyond the national in-group.

detail.abstract: Public cancer research funding is routinely described as disconnected from disease burden. This paper re-examines the claim for seventeen cancers accounting for USD 2,953 million of National Cancer Institute funding and 77 % of cancer deaths in the United States, and then for nine national project portfolios recorded in the International Cancer Research Partnership database. Funding does track mortality, with an elasticity of 0.93, but observed allocations typically deviate by a factor of two in either direction from a burden-proportional allocation. Three competing conceptions of the public objective, each evaluated separately without any calibrated parameter, define a common core of USD 265.5 million whose direction of reallocation does not depend on which conception is adopted. The density of patient advocacy, measured by the number of dedicated charitable organisations per cancer, accounts for 65.7 % of the variance of the residual gap; a nineteen-year panel shows that this relationship is a long-run state rather than a dynamic response. Advocacy is itself associated with social stigma: holding disease burden constant, cancers linked to disapproved behaviours have 76 % fewer organisations. Tested symmetrically across the nine portfolios, the widely cited thesis of a female disadvantage in health research yields the opposite result in oncology: female cancers account for a share of projects 7.94 percentage points higher than their share of burden in all nine countries, mainly because of breast cancer, which explains 86 % of the gap, while the prostate shows no significant deviation. Seven legitimate denominators yield three different answers to the sex question; the verdict depends on the denominator before it depends on the allocation.

detail.abstract: Purpose: We assessed whether EEG power spectral density (PSD) fluctuates across age, sex, hemisphere, and brain region. Subsequently, we examined how these measures correlate with seizure semiology and EEG profiles among people with active convulsive epilepsy in rural Kenya.Methods: Routine scalp EEGs were recorded in people with epilepsy between January and June 2009 (25–30 minutes; 10–20 electrodes), with hyperventilation and photic stimulation, unless contraindicated. Traces were clinically interpreted and classified as normal or abnormal, and localisation of abnormalities to specific brain regions was determined. EEG files were filtered and resampled, and PSD was estimated per channel using the Welch's method; absolute and relative band powers (delta, theta, alpha, beta) were compared across hemispheres and regions. Associations with clinical covariates were modelled. Results: Anatomically, absolute alpha power was significantly higher in the right compared to the left (median 4.94×10−12 vs 4.49×10−12; p=0.046). Regional differences were pronounced: delta peaked in frontal and temporal leads, while alpha was higher over occipital leads. Clinically, PSD measures showed limited discrimination between normal and abnormal EEGs; though relative alpha power was higher in normal recordings (p=0.051). While acute encephalopathy and learning difficulties correlated with abnormal recordings EEGs, specific histories showed localised PSD shifts. Status epilepticus was associated with increased parietal absolute power, and prior head injury with reduced relative power in central and occipital regions.Conclusion: PSD metrics reflected developmental and neurophysiological organization among people with epilepsy. These findings support further validation of quantitative EEG pipelines for epilepsy phenotyping in resource-limited settings.

detail.abstract: Offline payment in central-bank digital currency rests on a tamper-resistant secure element that holds a balance and enforces its own limits. This note argues that the balance-based variant-the one specified for the offline digital euro-turns a shared secure-element flaw into a capability for creating unbacked value at scale. Its main cost is paid once while its yield grows with the devices it reaches; it leaves no evidence attached to the affected value, so the issuer sees only a late aggregate discrepancy at redemption; and it leaves only responses applied to every holder the operator cannot rule out. The defender's necessary move then reproduces the disruption an adversary would seek, which makes this a question of economic security rather than residual cyber-risk. Drawing on Operation Bernhard, documented secure-element breaks and South Africa's prepaid-token fraud, the note sets out what value carrying an authenticated history of its own transfers would change, what it would not, and five questions for an economic-security assessment.

detail.abstract: In January 2024, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved the first spot Bitcoin ETFs, marking a milestone in the institutionalization of crypto asset markets. This paper examines how this regulatory event affected the market quality and price efficiency of Bitcoin spot markets. Using intraday trade and order book data from Coinbase and Kraken between November 2023 and March 2024, we apply a difference-indifferences framework with two control groups: Ether and the 30 Nasdaq-100 stocks most correlated with Bitcoin. We analyze volatility, trading activity, liquidity, and price efficiency. Rather than improvements in market quality due to the introduction of Bitcoin ETFs, we find that top-of-book depth deteriorates robustly relative to Ether, while trading volume rises substantially but only within U.S. trading hours, when ETF and Authorized Participant activity is concentrated. Volatility and price efficiency show no response, and direct measures of adverse selection do not increase. We interpret the liquidity deterioration as an inventory-risk rather than an information-based effect: the ETF channels large, uninformed demand into the spot market, making it busier but shallower.

detail.abstract: The Single-Stack 100/50 Principle defines two independent, formally derivable consequences of retiring the IPv4 protocol stack in a dual-stack (IPv4 + IPv6) network environment: (1) 100% elimination of executable attacks attributable to IPv4 under the paper's definition, and (2) an exact 50% reduction in the count of concurrently exposed network-layer protocol-stack surfaces when IPv4 is retired, stated by the Principle as a minimum structural floor. The analysis is bounded to the functional Layer 3 scope and parameter universe U₃ defined in this paper. Within that premise, Axiom 0 and Axioms 1-15 stipulate protocol independence, operational state transitions, traffic termination, addressing/routing domains, protocol-associated control and resolution functions, header-processing paths, and protocol-specific vulnerability execution. Theorem I follows by removal of the necessary IPv4 Layer 3 execution precondition for every IPv4-attributable attack. Theorem II follows by direct enumeration of two concurrently exposed protocol-stack surfaces before retirement and one after retirement. Neither theorem depends on empirical attack volume, incident frequency, or statistical inference, and neither theorem claims that IPv6 is inherently more secure than IPv4.

detail.abstract: This Article examines the evolution of AI liability litigation arising from the Tumbler Ridge tragedy, culminating in the September 2026 action brought by the Province of British Columbia and School District No. 59 against OpenAI entities and their leadership. It traces the shift from private family claims to public-entity litigation seeking both compensation and prospective changes to AI safety architecture. The Article argues that the central legal questions concern not artificial autonomy, but human and corporate control: who designed the system, who knew of the risk, who controlled escalation, and who possessed authority to act. On the allegations pleaded, the critical breakdown occurred not at the AI detection stage or human safety review, but at the level of corporate decision-making. The Article concludes that litigation is an indispensable but retrospective accountability mechanism. Effective AI governance therefore requires a federal ex ante framework establishing auditable risk detection, human escalation, incident reporting, record preservation, and non-delegable corporate responsibility.

detail.abstract:
The Jameel Binary Philosophy proposes a conceptual and philosophical framework that positions the binary system (0, 1) as the foundational grammar of existence, bridging classical metaphysics, modern physics, and Artificial Intelligence. It re-imagines 0 as Absolute Potential — the non-manifest, invisible essence (Ghayb) — and 1 as Manifestation, the point where potential crosses into matter, time, and action. The originality of the Jameel Binary Philosophy lies not in the binary system itself, but in proposing that philosophical causality can be translated into a Binary Assembly Code, enabling Artificial Intelligence to investigate reality under ethical guidance as a conceptual framework for future knowledge.

By encoding philosophical causality into a Binary Assembly Code, the framework proposes that AI can be directed to decode universal structures that lie beyond human sensory perception, including those identified at the Event Horizon by Susskind’s Holographic Principle and Wheeler’s ‘It from Bit’ thesis. The theory fulfils Leibniz’s 17th-century vision of a Characteristica Universalis and builds upon Judea Pearl’s causal mathematics and David Bohm’s Implicate Order. It is presented as a Principal Theory — a philosophical roadmap for future interdisciplinary investigation — rather than a completed empirical model. The paper concludes that we are entering the era of Informational Metaphysics, wherein AI becomes a telescope into the logical architecture of existence.

detail.abstract: Models of AI-driven automation typically treat the firm that automates and the workers it displaces as sharing a single labor market. This is increasingly unrealistic once tradable tasks are offshored across borders, as in business-process outsourcing, offshored IT-services delivery, and global capability centers. This paper extends the Acemoglu-Restrepo displacement-productivityreinstatement decomposition of automation's labor-demand effect to a two-block setting in which the economy automating a task (block N) and the economy supplying it (block S) can differ. We give the automating block's decision an explicit outside-option and bargaining structure, and derive, under a stated sequential benchmark timing, a counterintuitive result: greater bargaining power for the laborsupplying economy's suppliers can itself accelerate the buyer's incentive to automate the task away entirely. We treat the geographic split of reinstatement as an explicit, stated assumption rather than a derived law, and separate two distinct questions that are often conflated: whether the labor-supplying economy would itself choose a different automation level (a labor-demand automation gap), and whether the automation level that actually results leaves its labor demand below its own achievable benchmark (a labor-demand gap), showing these need not share a sign. We illustrate the mechanism across several sectors, with India's IT-services and global-capability-center sector as one case among others, and set out testable predictions and policy-relevant intervention margins.

detail.abstract: Neuroforecasting uses neural activity recorded from small laboratory samples to predict the aggregate behavior of much larger populations. Across at least sixteen fMRI studies spanning music sales, advertising, microlending, crowdfunding, news sharing, video engagement, equity markets, and mobile games, neural measures improve out-of-sample forecasts of market-level outcomes. In about half of these studies, they outperform self-report and incentivized choice collected from the same participants. Here we review this evidence and then discuss a theoretical explanation. We argue that valuation can be decomposed into components that differ in how much idiosyncratic variance they carry, and that neural measures forecast well when they isolate the components of value that generalize across people. A random utility model formalizes the argument, providing guidance on how large a brain sample must be relative to a survey sample, as a function of the idiosyncrasy carried by the neural signal and its measurement precision. We close with open questions about the identity of the shared psychological process and the potential dependence of its neural signature on different markets.

detail.abstract: Space-enabled technologies underpin communications, navigation, Earth observation, and critical infrastructure, yet most estimates of the space economy are revenue tallies built on proprietary classifications that ignore production linkages. We develop a reproducible accounting framework, based on publicly available U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis input–output tables, that measures the production-network footprint of a conservatively defined core space sector and separates direct core output from the indirect requirements connecting the core to suppliers and user industries. Indirect requirements exceed direct output in every benchmark year and grow faster: direct core output rose from $60 billion in 2007 to $78 billion in 2017 (2017 chain dollars), while indirect requirements rose from $83 billion to $125 billion, so that each dollar of core output was associated with $1.60 of cross-sector production requirements by 2017. The largest upstream requirements sit in communications infrastructure and business services rather than aerospace-specific inputs, and downstream dependence rises fastest in federal defense. In an illustrative projection to 2030, the baseline footprint reaches $350 billion, two-thirds of it indirect. Results are robust to a value-added mapping. The framework turns space-economy measurement from sizing a sector into mapping exposure and concentration in the infrastructure the economy increasingly runs on.

detail.abstract: Africa's digital challenge is no longer the absence of infrastructure. It is fragmentation: identities, payment rails, data environments, regulatory regimes and private-sector platforms that work well inside one country and stop at its border. This paper argues that interoperable digital public infrastructure (DPI) can form a single trusted digital layer across borders, and that this layer is what allows artificial intelligence to understand economic activity and enable seamless cross-border trade. We set out a layered model connecting physical infrastructure, DPI, interoperability, AI and trade applications. Using a Kigali to Nairobi transaction as a worked example, we show where the East African stack breaks today. We then define five interoperability layers, identity, payments, data, regulatory and behavioural, and describe how behavioural intelligence built on top of them can assess risk, detect fraud, personalise financial services and surface trade opportunities. We close with the safeguards this demands on surveillance, consent, privacy, bias and explainability.

detail.abstract: Across much of the humanitarian sector, artificial intelligence use-especially bottomup adoption by individual practitioners-is advancing faster than formal organizational governance and training. A 2025 survey of 2,539 humanitarian practitioners found that 70% used AI daily or weekly, while only 22% reported a formal organizational AI policy. In a separate January 2026 respondent sample of 1,729 practitioners, 75% reported daily or weekly use, 23.3% reported a formal policy and only 9% reported organizationwide integration. Because the surveys were self-selected and did not follow the same respondents, these figures indicate a recurring gap rather than a measured trend. This academic opinion paper argues that humanitarian organizations should adopt a minimum ethical floor as an interim decision rule rather than wait for a comprehensive framework. It proposes six governance conditions: legitimate humanitarian purpose and necessity; attributable institutional responsibility; meaningful human control; protection from data and model harms; transparency, participation and contestability; and continuing monitoring with a duty to stop. Before authorizing an AI-supported practice, an organization should document how each condition's core function will be performed. If it cannot do so, the use carries a strong presumption against authorization and should normally be redesigned, postponed or refused. This is a normative policy proposal derived from a structured synthesis of existing commitments, not an empirically validated rule, a statement of existing law or an established sector-wide prohibition. Emergency pressure may change the form and timing of evidence, but it does not remove the need to perform each governance function.

detail.abstract: This study examines how family ownership affects a firm's climate performance and how this effect is shaped by multinational enterprises' (MNEs') exposure to international institutional environments. Drawing on agency theory and the socioemotional wealth (SEW) perspective, we analyze Korean family-owned MNEs, which operate in a domestic context of institutional voids but interact with diverse global regulatory regimes. Using firm-level data on greenhouse gas emissions and foreign exchange-based measures of regional dependency, we find that concentrated family ownership is associated with weaker climate engagement. However, this relationship is context-dependent: internationalization mitigates the adverse effect of family ownership, especially when firms are exposed to environmentally stringent host countries. In contrast, exposure to institutionally lax environments reinforces or fails to offset this negative influence. No significant effects are found for intermediate levels of regulation. These findings show that family firms' climate behavior is shaped not only by ownership structure but also by transnational institutional pressures. International exposure thus emerges as a potential substitute for weak home-country governance in emerging markets.

detail.abstract: Tobacco production represents an important agricultural activity for a considerable number of farmers in North Macedonia, while its long-term sustainability is influenced by economic performance, government support, and the predictability and effectiveness of agricultural policies. detail.abstract:
New ventures commit to business concepts before the direction of their innovation ecosystems is fully revealed. However, familiar concepts are easier to evaluate but offer limited option value, whereas concepts that anticipate an emerging trajectory may offer greater returns but are harder to evaluate and protect. We introduce temporal positioning, a concept's orientation toward the ecosystem's emerging trajectory relative to its established concept base. Using 376,667 business descriptions from 1950 to 2023, we measure temporal positioning as the ratio of forward to backward textual similarity. Our theory weighs the benefits of trajectory alignment against evaluation costs and appropriability risks and predicts an inverted U-shaped relationship with initial financing. We test these predictions using three complementary datasets. First, detailed financing records for 37,916 ventures receiving venture capital in the United States allow us to examine capital commitment across industries. We find an inverted U association between temporal positioning and the amount raised in the first recorded financing round. The curve is flatter and peaks at higher temporal positioning in hotter industries and ecosystems with faster clockspeed. Forward positioning is associated with lower funding before comparable ventures enter, and this penalty diminishes as they arrive. These findings suggest that the value of forward positioning depends on the comparison evidence available when investors commit capital. Second, to probe the underlying mechanism, we leverage a competition dataset covering 2,669 business plans combines texts fixed at submission with 22,533 independent expert evaluations. Judges agree more when novelty and market potential are balanced, consistent with lower evaluation uncertainty. Third, we employ a dataset of 12,160 artificial intelligence (AI) products from a large AI product discovery platform to extend the analysis to a rapidly developing ecosystem, with users as evaluators and attention as the resource allocated. User saves increase with temporal positioning at a diminishing rate over most of the observed range, consistent with the prediction for faster concept turnover. Our findings link entrepreneurial entry timing to capital commitment through the evaluation of concepts within evolving ecosystems. They suggest that investors and venture platforms should consider the emergence of relevant comparison ventures when evaluating concepts and allocating capital.

detail.abstract: Right-sizing compute in a cloud data warehouse is a continuous, workload-specific exercise, and the two platforms this paper examines, Snowflake and Databricks, expose fundamentally different unit-economics for that exercise despite solving a similar underlying problem. This paper documents both platforms' native compute-sizing and billing mechanisms using official vendor documentation, and finds a structural difference more consequential than any single pricing figure: Snowflake bundles compute and platform fee into a single currency, credits, with an official, precisely documented ten-tier warehouse-size table from X-Small to 6X-Large in which credit consumption per hour exactly doubles at every size increase, from 1 credit per hour at X-Small to 512 credits per hour at 6X-Large, billed per second with a 60-second minimum each time a warehouse starts. We independently verify Snowflake's own published worked billing example across four running-time windows, reproducing its stated credit totals exactly. Databricks instead separates cost into two distinct lines: a Databricks Unit (DBU) platform fee, whose rate varies by cluster type (All-Purpose compute carrying the highest rate, Jobs compute lower, SQL compute serverless or classic), and a separately billed underlying cloud virtual machine cost charged directly by the cloud provider, meaning a single DBU-rate figure alone understates total compute spend. We synthesize this architectural contrast into a direct comparison, an empirical right-sizing decision framework accounting for each platform's specific scaling levers, and a proposed evaluation methodology for teams benchmarking their own workloads on either platform.

detail.abstract: The effects of decentralization on local development remain widely debated. Theory suggests that decentralization is most effective where local governments are of higher quality, yet causal evidence is scarce because government quality and local development are jointly determined. Exploiting a major decentralization reform in Italy and combining a factorial difference-in-differences design with new, rich local data, we identify how the returns to decentralization vary with government quality. We find that localities governed by higher-quality institutions experience substantially stronger long-run development. This effect starts only when the devolution process is fully implemented and, importantly, its gains are nonlinear: the largest returns arise when government quality improves from very low to intermediate levels, while further improvements generate markedly smaller additional benefits.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth in demand for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operations requires effective allocation of limited low-altitude airspace under dynamically arriving requests. When operating at scale, thousands of UAVs simultaneously compete for access to shared airspace resources, and capacity allocation becomes a central challenge for maintaining efficiency and safety. We study a real-time route allocation problem in which heterogeneous UAV requests compete for capacity on a spatiotemporal low-altitude airspace network, with the objective of maximizing social welfare while ensuring conflict-free operations under link-time capacity constraints. We formulate the problem as an online combinatorial allocation model and develop a pricing-based primal-dual algorithm that assigns route access using dynamically updated link-time unit price. In contrast to conventional ground and airspace traffic management rules, such as first-come-first-served and greedy admission rules, the proposed method assigns link-time unit price based on capacity usage, so the route access is granted only when the request's reported valuation exceeds the total price of the route. The method is computationally efficient and admits a provable performance guarantee relative to the offline optimum. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method achieves near-optimal system performance at scale and significantly outperforms conventional benchmark policies. Using large-scale delivery data from China, we show that coordinated UAV deployment reduces delivery times by 77.7% on average, with reductions exceeding 90.0% in first-and last-mile operations, and improves accessibility to time-sensitive services in remote and mountainous regions. These results demonstrate that capacity-aware, market-based allocation provides a tractable and effective framework for managing UAV traffic in low-altitude airspace.

detail.abstract: We study the real effects of China's 2021 administrative power rationing on manufacturing firms. Using an innovative plant-level measure of production based on satellite thermal infrared radiation (TIR) and the staggered adoption of city-level mandatory rationing, we implement a stacked differencein-differences design and estimate that rationing reduces plant activity by 16.7%. The effects are robust to a wide range of tests and are stronger in plants operated by private firms. Firms partly offset the shock by reallocating production across facilities and front-loading output. At the same time, the disruption propagates through production networks, as unaffected plants with rationed upstream suppliers reduce production. Exposed firms also experience negative short-term stock price reactions and reduce longrun capital expenditures. Overall, our results highlight both the intended and unintended consequences of China's "dual control" energy policy framework, and show how these outcomes are shaped by the interaction between government intervention and market forces.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a theory of autonomous-capital governance in labor-substituting artificial intelligence. When AI augments labor, firms manage adoption, training, workflow redesign, and human-AI complementarity. When AI substitutes for labor, AI systems become autonomous capital: productive assets that generate machine labor. This shift changes the central management problem from managing AI-enabled work to governing the ownership, access, claims, and control structures of the assets that increasingly perform work. I develop a model in which human participation and machine labor jointly produce output, and machine labor is produced by autonomous capital. As AI labor-substitutability rises, the share of value accruing to human labor falls while the share accruing to autonomous capital rises. When autonomous-capital ownership is concentrated, stakeholders who depend on labor, participation, or access-based income but hold weak claims on autonomous-capital surplus lose relative claims on value. The model shows that labor-substituting AI increases the value of shared claims, access infrastructure, and accountability because autonomous capital generates both surplus concentration and control power. However, because governance can impose incentive, administrative, and innovation costs, the optimal governance architecture is interior: private innovation remains active, while shared claims, access infrastructure, and accountability are positive. The paper contributes to AI strategy, platform governance, stakeholder theory, and innovation governance by showing that labor-substituting AI shifts the managerial problem from adopting AI tools to governing machine-labor-producing capital.

detail.abstract: In contemporary policy science literature, the category policy elite has become increasingly visible, particularly in research examining policymaking processes, governance networks, and elite interviewing. Despite its growing use, however, relatively little attention has been devoted to its conceptual foundations or its relationship with the extensive traditions of elite theory that have shaped social science scholarship in large and policy science scholarship in particular for more than a century. This article argues that the emergence of policy elite raises important ontological and epistemological questions that remain insufficiently addressed within contemporary policy research. Drawing upon the works of Mosca, Pareto, Michels, Mills, Lasswell, and Foucault, the paper examines the relationship between policy elites and established categories such as political, administrative, bureaucratic, technocratic, and epistemic elites. It argues that methodological discussions concerning the identification and study of policy elites have advanced more rapidly than conceptual discussions concerning the nature of the category itself. More broadly, the paper suggests that the growing reliance on policy elite may reflect a wider shift within policy studies from analysing power and authority towards analysing governance processes. The article calls for renewed engagement with elite theory, political power, and conceptual clarity in policy sciences.

detail.abstract: Jaguar Land Rover presents a striking strategic paradox. After several years of transformation, the company achieved a strong strategic and financial recovery while continuing to invest heavily in its future. Yet soon afterwards it was again under pressure and undertaking another major round of adjustment. This study examines how genuine adaptation can be difficult to sustain so quickly. Using a five-phase longitudinal case study from FY2015/16 to September 2026, it traces how Jaguar Land Rover's strategy, operations and financial position changed over time. The evidence shows that the earlier recovery was real, but the business built on it became harder to sustain as conditions changed and commitments continued. To explain this, the paper develops a Fit-Supportability-Durability (FSD) framework. Fit asks whether the strategic direction remains appropriate, Supportability whether the business can carry it, and Durability whether that ability can persist. Jaguar Land Rover's case poses a sharper question than why firms restructure: why did another major adjustment follow so soon after a recovery that had clearly worked?

detail.abstract: The tonne-mile metric serves as a measure to proxy demand for commodity transport in tramp shipping, yet predicting it is challenging due to complex trade route interdependencies and a dynamic geopolitical landscape. This study proposes a methodology for predicting tonne-miles based on trade flow modelling. Leveraging country-level export and import data, we frame tonne-mile estimation as a variant of the Minimum-Cost Flow Problem (MCFP) tailored towards tramp shipping and construct a time-expanded flow network that integrates multiple datasets to capture trade relationships. To evaluate the methodology, we perform a series of experiments across four key Clean Petroleum Product (CPP) commodities, demonstrating the ability of the model to reconstruct tonne-miles over a four-year historical period with a 2.1% Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Finally, we showcase our method's utility as a decision-support tool by estimating future tonne-miles under several market scenarios utilising projected country-level export and import data. The framework can be used to estimate tonne-miles per commodity segment both regularly and during disruptions, such as geopolitical tensions.

detail.abstract: Digital advertising platforms use auction-time autobidding alongside campaign-level controls over budgets and delivery. These two decision layers operate at different timescales and draw on different information, so their recommendations can diverge at execution. We address this coordination problem with an execution-boundary framework that varies both bidder discretion and the rule used to resolve bidder-controller disagreement while leaving both components unchanged. Across controlled simulations, latent-truth evaluations, and logged-auction replays, varying execution authority reveals a value-delivery tradeoff: much of the advertiser-value gain emerges at intermediate levels of discretion, while broader authority increasingly weakens budget delivery and eventually yields diminishing gains. The relative performance of coordination rules also depends on the campaign's delivery tolerance. Discretion is most valuable when bidder-controller disagreement is associated with better opportunity ranking relative to the campaign-control reference and when the campaign has enough replacement opportunities to redeploy budget preserved by selective rejection. Calibrating execution width by bidder and budget-supply scenario improves the valuedelivery balance relative to a common fixed width. In a shared-market reconstruction, execution width and adoption scale generate different market responses: advertiser gains coexist with lower clearing prices and current auction revenue, as well as spillovers to non-adopters. The results identify execution coordination as a platform operating decision whose appropriate configuration depends on campaign conditions, while its market consequences also depend on deployment scale.

detail.abstract: Retrospective back-tests are often used to argue that a forecasting method, including one built on large language models (LLMs), can anticipate technological change. Such tests are exposed to look-ahead problems: public prior art at the simulated cut-off T₀, cueing by the information supplied to the forecaster, hindsight in assembling that information, broad enumeration of competing branches, post-hoc choice of the resolution at which predictive credit is assigned, and latent post-T₀ knowledge in the model. We integrate these threats into an ordered validity protocol. It fixes the credited object and its architectural resolution first (Step 0) and uses that resolution unchanged when auditing public availability at T₀ (Step 1) and the construction and contents of the forecast input (Step 2); it then records forecast commitment and breadth (Step 3) and treats realization, selection and ranking as descriptive endpoints (Steps 4–6). For an LLM trained after T₀, a historically correct forecast is compatible both with inference from pre-T₀ information and with latent post-T₀ knowledge, so retrospective performance — for emergence, selection or ranking — is not identifiable without an independently controlled temporal knowledge boundary. We apply the protocol to nine medical-technology histories (27 locked assessments) from the Innovation DNA dossier. No case froze its credit object and resolution before outcome review, so, by construction, none can be confirmed as a clean emergence test (0 of 9). This is not a forecasting score: it means the series offers no valid denominator for estimating emergence-forecasting performance. The case-level audit is informative in a different way. In four cases the forecasts stayed within branches or architectures the input already supplied; in the other five, exclusion of at least one assessment depends on the resolution chosen, on a post-hoc recombination rule or on unresolved pack provenance. Retrospective foresight claims should be audited as information-boundary problems before they are scored for accuracy. A prospective feasibility implementation of the protocol was publicly registered on OSF Registries on 29 September 2026, before candidate extraction, case selection, case-specific question setting or forecasting; it is not part of the forecasting-performance evidence reported here.

detail.abstract: The quantitative instruments of modern finance, from calendars, life tables and least squares to the normal law, the random walk and rescaled-range analysis, were developed to describe natural systems that are indifferent to being predicted. This monograph argues that their migration into reflexive markets, where forecasts alter the behaviour they forecast, opens a reflexivity gap that institutions must manage rather than assume away. It reconstructs this lineage as a whole and proposes a five-dimension provenance audit, applied in the final chapters to machine learning in finance and to supervisors, central banks and investors. Four reproducible tests on public data spanning 622 to 2026 illustrate the argument. Monthly US equity returns since 1871 are fat-tailed, with Hill tail indices of 2.6 to 3.0. A naive variance-ratio test rejects the random walk in 12 of 12 cases, but in only 1 of 12 against a Monte Carlo null that reproduces the monthly averaging of the price series identified by Working (1960). An apparent sunspot-inflation correlation (p ≈ 0.01) fails a Bonferroni correction, reverses its timing and vanishes once war and oil-shock episodes are excluded. Long memory is present in the Nile (Roda gauge, 622-1284) and in market volatility, but not in returns. The monograph comprises 12 chapters, 21 tables, 5 figures and 89 verified references, and is accompanied by a full replication package of data, code, seeds and output tables.

detail.abstract:
Background: In high-volume public hospitals in India, complex, multi-step care pathways can create navigational barriers that delay care and burden patients and staff. Structured volunteer support could help address non-clinical barriers to accessing care. We evaluated SARATHI, a student-volunteer programme providing non-clinical navigation support in the outpatient departments of a tertiary hospital in north India.

Methods: In this mixed-methods evaluation, we compared SARATHI-assisted and non-assisted first-time adult outpatients across registration, consultation, diagnostic, and pharmacy (Jan Aushadhi Kendra) service points. Outcomes included navigation time, utilisation of services, and patient-reported experience, analysed using multivariable regression. Volunteers’ experiences were explored through a self-administered web-based questionnaire, analysed thematically.

Findings: Among 3074 participants, SARATHI assistance was associated with a 22·13-min reduction in adjusted navigation time (95% CI −28·07 to −16·18), concentrated in diagnostic services (−62·73 min, −70·14 to −55·32), with no difference at consultation (−0·36 min, −4·90 to 4·17). Thematic analysis identified four themes: personal transformation; transferable skills and practical exposure; value of patient support; and challenges and suggested improvements.

detail.abstract: A formulaic method is developed for periodic cash distributions made by a charitable foundation from a perpetuity endowment. The method achieves the greatest dollar disbursement amount while avoiding "ruin" with a specified probability. The method is "size aware" in that the percent disbursement depends on the value of the assets held by the endowment at the time of each disbursement. There are five inputs to the calculation: the real geometric mean of the rate of investment gain of the endowment assets; the standard deviation of that rate; the asset level that defines "ruin"; the probability of ruin; and the current value of the endowment assets. The endowment assets may include cash, equities, bonds, pledges, or loans (either as lender or borrower). Numerical examples illustrate the method.

detail.abstract: Public organizations face accelerating cyber and quantum threats that require workforce strategies grounded in measurable readiness, operational realism, and strategic agility. This conceptual paper develops a dual-evidence evaluation framework by integrating Banasiewicz's empirical-experiential evidence framework with Barends and Rousseau's evidence-based management framework. The model combines empirical indicators, including role adoption, certification rates, post-quantum cryptography readiness, and retention trends, with experiential evidence from leaders, training institutions, and research bodies. It provides a structured approach to assessing whether cyber workforce strategies translate into operational capability rather than merely generating compliant activities and reports. The framework helps senior leaders identify implementation gaps, assess emerging risks, and direct resources toward high-impact initiatives. It consists of a logic model, an evidence-scoring rubric, a leadership dashboard, quarterly assessment cycles, and risk-informed recommendations. Together, these components offer reusable architecture through which an agency can refine its workforce strategy as technologies, missions, and adversary capabilities evolve. The paper labels this integration a dual-evidence model and explains how it could strengthen strategic oversight and cyber workforce readiness.

detail.abstract: Nudge and boost are the two dominant classes of non-coercive behavioural intervention, and both have been imported into cybersecurity with limited adaptation. This paper argues that the import is unsound because both classes rest on assumptions that do not hold in the security domain. Nudge assumes a benevolent choice architect and a stable environment; boost assumes a learning environment kind enough for competence to be built and exercised. In cybersecurity, a hostile actor often authors the choice architecture, adapts faster than the defender, engineers time pressure and affect, and whose success is a rare, high-cost, low-feedback event. I argue that the nudge and boost taxonomy is organised on a single axis, what the intervention targets, and lacks a second axis that adversarial domains require: who designed the decision environment. Adding that axis opens a cell that neither class occupies. I introduce brace as the intervention class that fills it: a pre-committed, pre-rehearsed response, held collectively, installed before contact with a hostile choice architecture, whose causal pathway removes the decision at the moment of contact rather than steering it or informing it. Brace assembles inoculation theory, implementation intentions and self-nudging, but is defined by design constraints that boost theory would treat as defects: it is deliberately narrow, deliberately fixed, and deliberately non-deliberative at the point of use. The paper sets out the axis, the definition, a comparison with nudge and boost on eight dimensions, a four-part taxonomy, seven use cases, and five falsifiable propositions, including the prediction that braces show no load penalty under engineered pressure where boosts do. The contribution is conceptual: the map behavioural public policy has drawn is missing a dimension, and brace is what occupies the space it opens.

detail.abstract: This study aims to document and analyze the historical roles of the most prominent figures of the Kingdom of Bahrain, from the founding pioneers who laid the foundations of the modern state to the leaders of the present and future who lead the march of development and prosperity. Findings reveal that the historical legacy of Bahrain's figures can be classified into eight distinct categories: the founding pioneers, the great leaders, the pioneers of intellectual enlightenment, the institution builders, the military and security leaders, the government leadership from the Al Khalifa family, the deputy prime ministers, and the leaders of the present and future. detail.abstract: Packaging heat-seal defects can generate material waste, additional handling and production interruptions, but their economic significance depends on recovery capacity and accounting boundaries. This computational study asks under what operating and cost conditions indirect losses exceed direct material losses and which drivers most influence that relationship. A deterministic monthly model links production time, defect detection, permitted rework, disposal, incremental labour, catch-up capacity and unrecovered contribution. Material balances prevent successfully reworked food from being counted as complete disposal. Fixed overhead allocations are excluded from incremental economic losses, and probability-weighted recall exposure is reported separately. Four illustrative scenarios, a 2,187-combination uncertainty grid, one-factor sensitivity experiments and analytical verification cases were executed in Python. All numerical operating and cost inputs are explicit assumptions rather than estimates of typical food plants; literature supports the mechanisms and analytical distinctions. With early detection and sufficient spare capacity, simulated indirect operating costs were USD 2,687 against USD 6,711 of material waste, giving a ratio of 0.40. Removing catch-up capacity increased the economic ratio to 2.67, although the incremental cash ratio remained 0.15. A longer-stoppage scenario with partial recovery produced an economic ratio of 4.89. Across the bounded grid, economic ratios ranged from 0.041 to 138.204; these are designdependent sensitivity ranges, not confidence intervals. Defect frequency, contribution margin, interruption duration and product material cost produced the widest one-factor ratio ranges. Higher ratios sometimes reflected a smaller material-loss denominator rather than greater absolute loss. detail.abstract: Project-management research has generated extensive knowledge concerning governance frameworks, leadership styles, organisational capabilities, and complexity management. However, comparatively little attention has been devoted to isolating the invariant characteristics intrinsic to the project form itself-distinct from extrinsic organisational responses to scale, multi-actor coordination, and administrative oversight. Grounded in Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT) and Task Interdependence Theory, this paper deconstructs canonical project attributes into universal scope conditions of purposeful endeavours (𝐶 1-𝐶 4) and distinctive structural dynamics (𝐶 5-𝐶 6). To isolate project ontology, we introduce two asymmetric diagnostic reduction gates: the Single-Actor Test (𝑁 actor = 1) and the Single-Activity Test (𝑁 activity = 1). Applying these gates establishes a three-tiered micro-foundational hierarchy that distinguishes atomic operations, actions or activities (𝒫𝒱 = 0), pure solo projects (𝑁 actor = 1, 𝒫𝒱 > 0), and multi-actor organisational arrangements (𝑁 actor > 1, 𝒫𝒱 > 0). From this analytical reduction, we derive five invariant first principles (𝑃 1-𝑃 5), demonstrating that projects are fundamentally systems of targeted state transformation (𝑆 0 → 𝑆 1) directed through multi-criteria decision-making across interdependent decision domains. Building on these principles, we propose the Plus-Shaped Project Management Model, an orthogonal architecture intersecting an ascending vertical transformation continuum with a horizontal spectrum of decision domains. Resonating with Morris's Management of Projects perspective, the model positions project management at the central locus, functioning primarily to maintain cross-domain decision integration throughout state transformation. Finally, the paper details a diagnostic framework for project simplification, explores implications for AIaugmented project environments, and establishes an empirical research agenda incorporating reference-class domain signatures.

detail.abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) reservation platforms allow customers to make reservations ahead of time. However, the assets are provided by independent \emph{hosts} who decide whether and when to list their assets on the platform, after considering the advance-booking and just-in-time markets. A high advance-booking price can incentivize hosts to list early, but may discourage customers from booking in advance, whereas a low price can fail to attract hosts to list early. We study whether a platform can sustain an advance-booking market and identify the conditions under which it instead collapses to a pure just-in-time market. We then examine whether granting hosts control over both prices and listing times mitigates this collapse. Motivated by data from a large car-sharing platform, we develop a two-period game-theoretic model of a P2P platform that sets the prices for both advance-booking and just-in-time customers. Hosts have private costs and face uncertainty about future asset availability when deciding when to list their assets. We show that hosts list early only if the advance price compensates them for their private fulfillment cost, the expected cancellation penalty, and the continuation value of waiting for the just-in-time market. As the just-in-time market becomes more attractive, there is no advance price that can simultaneously attract early supply and advance-booking customers, i.e., the platform collapses to a just-in-time market. We show that if hosts face a positive cancellation penalty or advance-booking customers have a lower maximum willingness to pay than just-in-time customers, then the collapse occurs at a finite level of just-in-time demand. Finally, we show that granting hosts pricing autonomy does not mitigate the collapse and, in fact, weakly expands the collapse region under mild conditions.

detail.abstract: Human resource management (HRM) is becoming a more modern and broader concept. It is no longer just about administering the workforce; it is about supporting employees on their wellness journey, promoting sustainable employment practices, and delivering outcomes for wider stakeholders. Thus, sustainable HRM is emerging as a framework for understanding employment practices that can help achieve social, environmental, and organizational goals. This article reviews the effectiveness of HR practices in ensuring social compliance and labor standards in the workplace, and how they affect employee well-being, organizational sustainability, and business performance. Based on a systematic review of peer-reviewed research, the study synthesizes evidence on the relationship between HR practices, employee well-being, high-performance work systems, sustainable HRM, and organizational outcomes. The findings show that HR practices, including employee participation, fair employment practices, leadership, supportive organizational environments, and development opportunities, can influence employee well-being and organizational performance. The synthesis also indicates that social compliance and labor standards are most effective when integrated into broader HR processes rather than treated as separate compliance requirements. Furthermore, employee well-being, engagement, organizational sustainability, and business performance appear to be interconnected outcomes influenced by the design and implementation of HR systems. The study proposes an integrated conceptual framework linking effective HR practices, workplace social compliance, employee well-being, organizational sustainability, and business performance. The framework highlights the importance of responsible employment practices, employee voice, fairness, safety, development, and organizational accountability in supporting sustainable workforce outcomes. The paper concludes that socially responsible HR practices can provide a foundation for building compliant, sustainable, and high-performing organizations, while recognizing that the strength of these relationships depends on organizational context and implementation.

detail.abstract: Strategic foresight commonly holds that crises announce themselves through weak anomalies appearing across several domains at once, and that their convergence carries more warning value than any single signal. The proposition underpins the indications-and-warning tradition and recent hybrid-threat frameworks, and it has rarely been tested against data, almost never against periods in which the signals appeared and no crisis followed. This study tests one concrete reading of it: alert when two or more domains are anomalous within four weeks. Six series - political violence, armed conflict, cyber incidents, maritime chokepoint traffic, naval posture and gas inflows - were assembled into a weekly panel of 6,750 area-weeks covering the Central and Eastern Mediterranean, North Africa and the Red Sea approaches from 2018 to 2026. Eleven cases were frozen before analysis: six crises, four comparable periods of tension in which no escalation followed, and one validation case. Thresholds, horizons, the reporting lag and the falsification conditions were fixed in writing before the first result; the analysis departed from that protocol in nine places, all stated, the most consequential being the choice of headline statistic. The alert rate in the twenty-six weeks before escalation is 10.3 per cent, against 10.4 per cent before the negative cases and 9.6 per cent in control weeks, and the pattern holds across every pre-committed specification. It also holds when the thresholds are estimated only from weeks before each case, when they are refitted on the literal control definition, and when cyber incidents are dated by their public attribution rather than by the day they began. Because chokepoint and naval-posture series are shared across areas, each case was also compared, as an exploratory check, with the control areas in the same weeks: there the crises alert at 10.3 per cent against 10.9. One reading changes the picture and is reported beside it: under the letter of the frozen definition, which makes the Tunisian negative a positive, the pre-crisis rate is 13.6 per cent and the negative rate 2.8, a borderline result that rests on that one case. Measured in the same unit and at the frozen thresholds, convergence identifies as many crises as its strongest single component, political violence; the protocol's own comparison between them cannot be decided on six cases - at an equal number of false-alarm episodes each catches five of the six - and neither rule separates the weeks before a crisis from control weeks. The 145 admissible pre-crisis weeks give 80 per cent power only for an effect at or above 1.76 times the control rate, under independence assumptions the paper rejects, so a moderate warning effect is not excluded. The validation case, the attack of 7 October 2023, would have been flagged in 12 of its 25 prior weeks, on cyber, protest, conflict and naval-posture signals between April and September 2023 whose relation to the attack this study does not test. Adding a seventh domain, air traffic, appeared to double the pre-crisis rate until the anomalies were partitioned by date, at which point the gain proved to be the 2020 collapse in civil aviation. Three findings about the sources matter at least as much. The two free products of the OpenSky aircraft-tracking network available to this study cannot see the theatre in question: one daytime hour yields 873 distinct aircraft over Italy and two over Libya. Publication time, which an honest backtest requires, is recorded natively in two of the six domains, and in one of them for just over half of the records. And the principal public archive for the information environment was withdrawn during the study. Whether these constraints explain the rule's failure to discriminate is not established; that any system built on these sources would meet them is.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: Growing demand for shared e-bike services increases battery replenishment needs and strains centralized charging operations. Deploying battery swapping cabinets across urban service regions offers a promising decentralized alternative. However, the effectiveness of battery swapping cabinets depends on riders' preferences for e-bikes with different battery levels and the coordination of battery swapping with fleet repositioning. In this paper, we study how to design a battery swapping network to improve battery replenishment in shared e-bike systems. Methodology/results: We develop an integrated optimization model that jointly determines battery swapping network design and operating decisions within a queueing network. Based on observed e-bike pickup patterns, we introduce an aggregate highest-energy-first-out (A-HEFO) rule to characterize riders' pickup behavior across battery levels. The resulting model is approximated by a tractable mixed-integer second-order cone program and evaluated using Capital Bikeshare data from Washington, DC. Managerial implications: We obtain the following findings. (i) In contrast to the conventional wisdom of inventory pooling, the decentralized battery swapping mode considerably reduces battery inventory and increases profitability relative to the centralized battery swapping mode. (ii) Accounting for riders' battery-level preferences is important for fleet operators. As riders become more sensitive to battery levels, the platform primarily responds by expanding its fleet, while battery inventory remains nearly unchanged. (iii) Crowdsourced repositioning can improve profitability, but its coordination with platform repositioning should account for cabinet presence at the destination, e-bike battery level, and incentive cost. (iv) Proactive battery swapping achieves the highest profitability, whereas a 20% threshold-activated swapping policy offers a practical alternative by achieving a slightly higher demand satisfaction rate without incurring a significant profit loss. (v) Among battery technology improvements, faster charging is more effective than greater battery capacity in accommodating e-bike demand growth.

detail.abstract: The NBD-Dirichlet implies a lower bound on the purchase frequency of a vanishingly small brand. This floor has a closed form that depends only on the Dirichlet parameter 𝑆 and the distribution of category purchases, so no brand parameter can move it. detail.abstract: The shift from mass, campaign-based advertising toward continuously learning, datadriven promotion marks a structural change in how organizations communicate value.
